input.quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
input.rationale: The Agreement grants TrueLink no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right against Client, and no right of access to Client systems for usage verification: searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "verify", "monitor" and "books" return nothing, and the Compensation (§ 5–6) and Client covenant (§ 8) sections contain only Client-favourable rights (§ 6 gives Client, not TrueLink, the right to supporting documentation and to contest charges; § 2.e gives Client real-time access to usage statistics and log files). With no audit right binding us, the position is better than the playbook's preferred limits (annual audit, 30 days' notice, vendor cost, no system access), so there is nothing to constrain and no redline is warranted. Noted only for awareness: § 8.f lets TrueLink "implement technical mechanisms" to prevent spamming, but that is an enforcement measure on TrueLink's own Interface rather than an audit or inspection of Client's systems or records, and it is addressed under the acceptable-use rules rather than here.
